question: When is a crossbleed engine start used?

options.text: When a normal APU bleed start is not possible, usually because the APU is inoperative
When the external power is not available

explanation: Air from the running engine is used to start the second engine.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In a crossbleed start, why is the receiving engine's ENG BLEED selected OFF?

options.text: To prevent the running engine's air escaping back through the receiving engine
To keep the receiving engine's pack running
To protect the receiving engine from overheat

explanation: With the bleed valve closed, the air goes to the start valve instead of leaking out through the bleed duct.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Where is the X BLEED selector set for a crossbleed engine start?
explanation: The cross bleed valve must be open to join the running engine's duct to the other side.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What minimum bleed pressure is required before attempting a start from a crossbleed or an air start unit?
explanation: If the pressure is lower, the running engine's thrust is increased (or the ASU checked) before starting.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: During a crossbleed start, what pressure should be maintained throughout?
explanation: Pressure often drops as the start valve opens; thrust is added on the supplying engine to keep at least 25 psi.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: During a crossbleed start, the supplying engine needs about 40 % N1 to keep the pressure. What should the crew consider?

options.text: Selecting the receiving engine bleed ON
Checking the area behind is clear and, if more than 40 % is needed, aborting as the configuration may be wrong

explanation: Needing much power suggests a leak or wrong valve setting, and jet blast becomes a hazard to people behind.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: After a crossbleed start, what happens to the X BLEED selector?

options.text: It stays OPEN for the flight
It is left in any position

explanation: After both engines run: supplying engine to idle, X BLEED to AUTO, receiving ENG BLEED back ON.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When should a crossbleed engine start not be performed?

options.text: During pushback, or where the engine's thrust would endanger people or property

explanation: The supplying engine needs significant thrust, which is dangerous behind the aircraft.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Why is external electrical power required for an air start unit (ASU) start?

options.text: Because the ASU needs electrical power to run
Because the engine starter is electric
Because the inoperative APU is not supplying electrical power

explanation: The ASU supplies air only; electrical power has to come from a ground power unit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Before an ASU is connected, how are the packs and the X BLEED selector set?

options.text: Both packs ON and X BLEED AUTO
Both packs OFF and X BLEED OPEN, with all bleeds OFF
Packs ON and X BLEED CLOSE
Packs OFF and X BLEED CLOSE

explanation: All the ASU's air must go to the starter, so nothing else draws on it.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In which position is the ENG MODE selector for normal operation?
explanation: IGN/START is used for starting on the ground and continuous ignition in flight.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does selecting ENG MODE to IGN/START do in flight?

options.text: It provides continuous ignition as required
It starts an in-flight relight automatically on both engines
Nothing; it works only on the ground

explanation: On the ground it starts the automatic or manual start sequence.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With ENG MODE at CRANK and ENG MAN START ON, what happens?

options.text: The start valve opens but the ignition does not fire
The fuel valve opens to purge the engine

explanation: Cranking turns the engine with the starter only.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does setting an ENG MASTER lever to ON do?

options.text: Opens only the low-pressure fuel valve
Tells the FADEC to start the automatic or manual start sequence

explanation: The start sequence follows the ENG MAN START pushbutton position.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does setting an ENG MASTER lever to OFF do?

options.text: Shuts the engine down or aborts its start sequence

explanation: It is the normal shutdown control.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which condition turns on the FAULT light on the pedestal ENG panel?

options.text: An automatic start sequence being aborted

explanation: FAULT also shows an HP fuel shut-off valve in an abnormal position or a thrust control malfunction. FIRE has its own light.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With ENG MODE at CRANK, ENG MASTER ON and ENG MAN START ON, what process takes place?
explanation: Master ON adds fuel, without ignition — a wet crank.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With ENG MODE at CRANK, ENG MASTER OFF and ENG MAN START ON, what process takes place?
explanation: No fuel and no ignition: the starter just turns the engine.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On which engines are the N1 MODE pushbuttons fitted?
explanation: N1 mode switches thrust control from EPR to N1 in an abnormal situation.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In N1 unrated (degraded) mode, what protection is lost?

options.text: The engine cannot reach take-off thrust
The thrust lever detents no longer protect the limits, so overboost is possible

explanation: N1 then follows thrust lever position only.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: How many FADECs control each engine?

options.text: One FADEC dedicated to each engine

explanation: Each FADEC controls and limits its own engine.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Does the autothrust move the A320's thrust levers?

options.text: No, they can only be moved manually

explanation: The levers set a limit; the A/THR controls the thrust within it.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: If a thrust lever is placed between two detents, which rating limit does the FADEC select?

options.text: The rating of the higher detent
The rating of the lower detent

explanation: The FADEC always takes the next detent up as the limit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: For a FLEX take-off thrust to be effective, the FLEX temperature must be higher than what?
explanation: Without a valid FLEX temperature, the FLX/MCT detent gives MCT on the ground.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ground, with no valid FLEX temperature set, what thrust does the FLX/MCT detent give?
explanation: A FLEX temperature is needed for reduced take-off thrust.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: After a FLEX take-off, can the crew return to FLEX thrust once they have moved the lever to TOGA or CL?

options.text: Yes, by returning to the FLX/MCT detent

explanation: Moving the lever out of FLX/MCT without reaching TOGA or CL has no effect.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: How can MAX take-off thrust always be obtained?

options.text: By pushing the thrust levers fully forward

explanation: TOGA is always available to the pilot.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What happens if one A/THR instinctive disconnect pushbutton is held for more than 15 seconds?

options.text: The A/THR is disconnected for the rest of the flight, including alpha floor
Only that engine's A/THR is lost
Nothing more than a normal disconnection

explanation: It can only be recovered at the next FMGC power-up on the ground.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: In autothrust, what limits the thrust the FMGC can command (outside alpha floor)?
explanation: The levers set the maximum; alpha floor is the exception.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ENG page, when is the fuel filter clog indication displayed?

options.text: When the fuel used is high
When the pressure loss across the fuel filter is excessive
When the fuel flow is low

explanation: It is hidden when the filter pressure is normal.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When does the oil quantity pulse on the ENG page?

options.text: When it is above the maximum
When it is below the oil advisory limit

explanation: Pulsing is an advisory, before any caution.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does a red oil pressure value on the ENG page mean?

options.text: The oil pressure is high but acceptable
The oil pressure is in the red range

explanation: Amber is the amber range; red is the red (limit) range.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When are the N1 and N2 vibration values shown in amber on the ENG page?

options.text: Whenever the engine is at take-off thrust
When the engine is in reverse
When the rotor vibration is excessive

explanation: Vibration is an advisory parameter for each rotor.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does A FLOOR on the E/WD indicate?

options.text: The alpha floor protection is active
The angle of attack sensors have failed

explanation: It appears near the thrust rating display.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which thrust rating is shown on the E/WD as MREV?
explanation: Other ratings include TOGA, MCT, CLB, FLX, derated take-off and GA SOFT.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What thrust rating does GA SOFT on the E/WD refer to?

options.text: Take-off thrust on a contaminated runway

explanation: A soft go-around uses less than full TOGA thrust.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is IDLE shown on the E/WD?

options.text: When either engine is at idle on the ground
When both engines are at idle in flight
When the APU is at idle

explanation: It helps the crew notice that thrust is at idle in the descent.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does an amber REV on the E/WD mean?

options.text: Reverse is selected on the ground

explanation: Green REV means fully deployed.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the A320neo E/WD, above what N1 is the value shown in red?
explanation: Exceeding the N1 limit is amber; beyond the 104 % red line it is red.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does the blue circle on the N1 gauge show?
explanation: The amber mark is the N1 limit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is the N2 value shown in a grey box on the E/WD?

options.text: When N2 is above the red line
When the engine is shut down
When the engine is in its start sequence or being cranked

explanation: The grey box disappears once the engine is started.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the A320neo E/WD, above what N2 is the value shown in red?
explanation: N2 has a red limit of 100 %.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.
